I checked this independently in polar coordinates centered at $O$. With $O$ at the origin, the hexagon subtends angles from about $19.1^\circ$ to $60^\circ$. Its nearest point is $S$ (distance $2\sqrt{3}$), and its farthest is $U$ (distance $\sqrt{52}$). Integrating $\tfrac12(R_{\text{out}}^2 - R_{\text{in}}^2)\,d\varphi$ over the swept angles $[19.1^\circ, 105^\circ]$ gives:

- Outer boundary contribution: $6\sqrt{3}$ (edges $AT$, $TU$) $+\ \tfrac{13\pi}{2}$ (sector of radius $\sqrt{52}$) $+\ 3\sqrt{3}$ (edge $UR$) $= 9\sqrt{3} + \tfrac{13\pi}{2}$.
- Inner boundary contribution: $\sqrt{3}$ (edge $SA$) $+\ \tfrac{3\pi}{2}$ (sector of radius $2\sqrt{3}$) $+\ 2\sqrt{3}$ (edge $SN$) $= 3\sqrt{3} + \tfrac{3\pi}{2}$.

The difference is $6\sqrt{3} + 5\pi$.
